headline: Approved conditional use permit for a personal fitness studio at 381 Main St, 7-0; two appointments tabled.
summary: Nick Braley and Eric Bobish plan a private personal training studio at 381 Main St, by appointment only. Neighbors raised concerns about traffic and hours, and the property owners said they are willing to add a stop sign and a stop bar. Two appointments were tabled to December 3, 2026, and 2027 meeting dates were accepted.
decisions: Approved the October 15, 2026 meeting minutes, as amended, 6-0-1, with Green abstaining.
Approved waiver of the site plan requirement for conditional use permit A26-0203, 7-0.
Approved conditional use permit for a personal fitness studio at 381 Main St, 7-0, with a condition to address outstanding Engineering comments.
Tabled appointment of a board member to the Nashua Regional Planning Commission Executive Committee to December 3, 2026.
Tabled appointment of a board member to the Historic District Commission to December 3, 2026.
Approved 2027 meeting and deadline dates, with the July 1st meeting changed to July 15th, 7-0.

EXPANDED DRAFT MEETING SUMMARY 
THIS IS NOT AN OFFICIAL TRANSCRIPT OF TAPE RECORDED PROCEEDINGS 
THE INFORMATION CONTAINED HEREIN HAS NOT BEEN REVIEWED OR APPROVED BY THE NCPB 
 
NASHUA CITY PLANNING BOARD 
November 19, 2026 
 
The regularly scheduled meeting of the Nashua City Planning Board 
was held on November 19, 2026 at 7:00PM in the 3rd floor auditorium 
in City Hall. 
 
Note: Video recording of this meeting is unavailable.  
 
Members Present: Joe MacIntyre, Mayor’s Representative 
 Bob Bollinger, Chair 
 Adam Varley, Vice Chair 
 Cameron Green, Clerk 
 Ald. Patricia Klee 
 Larry Hirsch 
 Benjamin Zoller 
   
Also Present: Sam Durfee, Planning Manager 
 Connor Muise, Deputy Planning Manager 
 Scott McPhie, Planner I 
  
APPROVAL OF MINUTES 
 
October 15, 2026 
 
MOTION by Ald. Klee to approve the minutes, as amended. 
 
SECONDED by Mr. Zoller 
 
MOTION CARRIED 6-0-1 (Green abstained) 
 
COMMUNICATIONS 
 
• A26-0203, 381 Main St 
o Updated Engineering comments 
• Discussion Item: Approval Criteria Presentation 
 
REPORT OF CHAIR, COMMITTEE, & LIAISON 
 
None 
 
PROCEDURES OF THE MEETING 
 
After the legal notice of each conditional, special use permit, 
site plan or subdivision plan is read by the Chair, the Board will 
determine if that the application is complete and ready for the
NCPB 
November 19, 2026 
Page 2 
 
Board to take jurisdiction. The public hearing will begin at which 
time the applicant or representative will be given time to present 
an overview and description of their project. The applicant shall 
speak to whether or not they agree with recommended staff 
stipulations. The Board will then have an opportunity to ask 
questions of the applicant or staff. 
 
The Chair will then ask for testimony from the audience. First 
anyone wishing to speak in opposition or with concern to the plan 
may speak. Please come forward to the microphone, state their name 
and address for the record. This would be the time to ask questions 
they may have regarding the plan. Next public testimony will come 
from anyone wishing to speak in favor of the plan. The applicant 
will then be allowed a rebuttal period at which time they shall 
speak to any issues or concerns raised by prior public testimony. 
 
One public member will then be granted an opportunity to speak to 
those issues brought by the applicant during their rebuttal period. 
The Board will then ask any relevant follow-up questions of the 
applicant if need be. 
 
After this is completed the public hearing will end and the Board 
will resume the public meeting at which time the Board will 
deliberate and vote on the application before us. The Board asks 
that both sides keep their remarks to the subject at hand and try 
not to repeat what has already been said. 
 
Above all, the Board wants to be fair to everyone and make the 
best possible decision based on the testimony presented and all 
applicable approval criteria established in the Nashua Revised 
Ordinances for conditional, special use permits, site plans and 
subdivisions. Thank you for your interest and courteous attention. 
Please turn off your cell phones and pagers at this time. 
 
Per our legal charter, we have a quorum when five members are 
present. There may be some recusals this evening for certain board 
members, but as long as five members are sitting each case can be 
heard. At the discretion of the chair, the order of the cases can 
be rearranged.  
 
NEW BUSINESS – CONDITIONAL USE PERMITS 
A26-0203  FMP Realty, LLC (Owner), Nick Braley (Applicant) 
requesting Conditional Use Permit approval for a 
personal fitness studio. Property is located at 381 Main
NCPB 
November 19, 2026 
Page 3 
 
Street, Unit 2. Map 109 Lot 7. Zoned A-Urban Residence 
(R-A). Ward 6. 
 
MOTION by Ald. Klee that the application is complete and the 
Planning Board is ready to take jurisdiction 
 
SECONDED by Mr. Hirsch 
 
MOTION CARRIED 7-0 
 
Nick Braley, 55 Concord St, Nashua NH 
 
Mr. Braley introduced himself to the Board. With him is Eric 
Bobish. They are planning to start a private personal training 
facility. At max there will be 3 trainers and their clients, so 5-
6 people at any time. This will be appointment only, no loud music. 
We have been operating since 2017 and we are both fully booked. 
We’re not looking to add clientele, just a new facility.  
 
Mr. Bollinger asked about hours of operation.  
 
Mr. Braley said they each have their own personal hours. He trains 
clients from 5:30AM-4PM. 
 
Mr. Bobish said his hours vary by day. He trains from 5:30-6AM to 
3:30-6PM.  
 
Mr. Bollinger asked if this was a 24-hour operation.  
 
Mr. Braley said no.  
 
Mr. Bobish said there’s no open door, no membership. People can’t 
come and go as they please, it’s by appointment only.  
 
Mr. Bollinger asked to discuss the waiver request. 
 
Mr. Braley said they are asking for a waiver from the preparation 
of a full site plan. There are no changes proposed to the site and 
the extent of the business doesn’t warrant it.  
 
Mr. Bollinger asked if they are keeping the same physical 
footprint. 
 
Mr. Braley said yes.  
 
Mr. Bollinger asked if they are not modifying the space.
NCPB 
November 19, 2026 
Page 4 
 
Mr. Braley said just paint, making it look a little prettier.  
 
Mr. Bollinger said the site plan of record was included, he has no 
issues with granting that waiver. He asked if the applicant can 
give an overview of the conditional use permit criteria.  
 
Mr. Braley provided a brief description of each criteria, as 
detailed in the case materials.  
 
Mr. Bollinger said the letter from Engineering concurred with their 
statement of traffic, and have waived the traffic contribution. He 
asked if they are okay with the conditions stipulated, a stop sign 
and bar, and a video of the sewer line.  
 
Mr. Braley said he doesn’t have a problem with it, but it’s not 
his property. He would have to ask the property owner. 
 
Mr. Bollinger said Engineering is also asking for a video of the 
sewer connection. If the owner is here, they are welcome to speak.  
 
Sharon Parent, 381 Main St, Nashua NH 
 
Ms. Parent said she has no issue with a stop bar or sign.  
 
Eric Parent, 381 Main St, Nashua NH 
 
Mr. Parent said the sewer system item is a suggestion, not 
required.  
 
Mr. Bollinger said he wants to make them aware of what was written. 
 
Mr. Parent said he is aware. He is not concerned with the condition 
of the sewer system. 
 
Mr. Bollinger said they are both technically recommendations, he 
wanted to bring it to the record. He recommends they follow-up 
with Engineering, he wanted it on the record. 
 
Mr. Parent said he has no problem with that.  
 
Ms. Parent said there will be no additional people coming into 
this business than there were for the office use. It’s small scale.  
 
Mr. Bollinger said he understands, it’s more about the conveyance 
of the message. We’ve had applicants that have not read or received 
Engineering comments. These are recommendations, not requirements.
NCPB 
November 19, 2026 
Page 5 
 
 
Ms. Parent said we can do the stop sign. It’s a very high traffic 
area, people get impatient.  
 
Ald. Klee said her concern is that the sewer system is from the 
1980s. You don’t want to suddenly have a backup. She is glad they 
are willing to do the stop bar and sign. This application is fine, 
the use is appropriate for the area.  
 
Mr. MacIntyre said the owners were clear that this is a 
recommendation, not a requirement. And they are willing to do a 
sign, maybe a bar.  
 
Mr. Parent said that’s just a painted line, they can do that. It’s 
not an issue.  
 
Ms. Sharon said there used to be a “no left turn” sign. She bought 
the property in 2019.  
 
Mr. MacIntyre asked if they have a concern on the recommendation 
of the sewer inspection.  
 
Mr. Parent said no. He doesn’t see the need for the sewer camera. 
He knows this building well, it’s a cast iron sewer line with no 
trees. There’s nothing to get in the way or cause issues. What 
this business is doing there is no different than what has been 
there before.  
 
Mr. MacIntyre said he understands. Does he have a problem with the 
recommendation of a sewer line inspection? 
 
Mr. Parent said no. He doesn’t want to spend the money on an 
inspection he doesn’t think it needs. If Engineering forces him to 
do it he will. 
 
Mr. MacIntyre asked if he had intentions of taking action on it.  
 
Mr. Parent said no. He doesn’t see a need for it.  
 
Mr. MacIntyre said we may follow up with Engineering on how they 
write reports, and recommendations versus the intention.  
 
Mr. Parent said exactly. If they required it, he would do it. But 
as it is a recommendation, it is not a requirement.
NCPB 
November 19, 2026 
Page 6 
 
Mr. MacIntyre said he thinks the use is compatible with the 
neighborhood. He hopes they have a good successful business there. 
How did they find this site, and where were they before? 
 
Mr. Braley said Ms. Parent is his client. He’s on Amherst Street 
right now, it just worked out that she was willing to make this 
happen. She wanted something compatible with her salon.  
 
Mr. Bollinger said he recommends they reach out to Mr. Mendola and 
seek a distinction on whether he intended it to be a recommendation 
or a requirement. We don’t want to see you spend money that you 
don’t need to. We’re not going to get hung up, the stipulation is 
that you have to address the matter with Public Works and 
Engineering. If that’s as simple as a follow-up call, that can be 
resolved outside of this meeting.  
 
Mr. Parent said he had the same thing done when he added four 
apartments at 23-27 Main Street. When the city required it, he did 
it and gave them the findings.  
 
Mr. Bollinger said because the wording of two the stipulations in 
the staff report were recommendations, it would be incumbent on 
the property owners to follow up with Engineering. We can’t 
determine that tonight, we’re not going to be the intermediary 
between the two.  
 
Mr. Parent said that’s fine.  
 
Mr. Zoller asked if they aren’t changing any of the plumbing 
inside, that was the fourth comment in the Engineering letter.  
 
Mr. Braley said they aren’t changing anything, it’s the exact same. 
 
SPEAKING IN OPPOSITION OR CONCERN 
 
Clayton Proffer, 2 Steven St, Nashua NH 
 
Mr. Proffer said he thinks it’s great that the space is going to 
be utilized, his only concerns were the hours of operation, volume 
of clients, and traffic. He shares an access easement for a 
driveway with this property.  
 
Brian O’Donnell, 379 Main St, Nashua NH
NCPB 
November 19, 2026 
Page 7 
 
Mr. O’Donnell said his only concern would be the traffic. After 
this discussion with the owners and the business, it doesn’t seem 
to be an issue. No concerns there.  
 
SPEAKING IN FAVOR 
 
None 
 
APPLICANT REBUTTAL 
 
None 
 
Mr. Bollinger said it seems that the neighbors had some concerns 
and that they were addressed by the meeting. He doesn’t mean this 
facetiously, but it’s nice when neighbors can get along and work 
out issues. He hopes all answers were provided this evening.  
 
PUBLIC MEETING 
 
Mr. Bollinger closed the public hearing and moved into the public 
meeting. He said this seems fairly straightforward, they gave a 
detailed overview. He thinks there may have been ambiguity in the 
Engineering letter, but the owner will follow-up to resolve that. 
Beyond that, he thinks the case for the waiver is straightforward 
and they satisfy the conditional use permit criteria.  
 
Ald. Klee said she doesn’t think there will be more traffic than 
was already there. The fact that they are willing to put up a stop 
sign and bar should help anyone coming in and out. The “no left 
turn” sign was probably because of the amount of traffic going out 
of there, she wonders if it was the city that did it.  
 
Ald. Klee asked staff if the stop bar would be required to be 
maintained, they go away over time. 
 
Mr. Durfee said that would be the assumption, that it would need 
to be maintained to serve the function.  
 
Ald. Klee said she sees no reason not to approve this.  
 
Mr. Zoller said there is a mixed-use zone not far from this site, 
and there are all sorts of businesses up and down Main St. Does it 
make sense to put an overlay in place on Main St for these 
commercial uses? 
 
Mr. Durfee said we’re working on a code update.
NCPB 
November 19, 2026 
Page 8 
 
 
MOTION by Mr. Green to approve the following waivers for New 
Business – Conditional Use Permit A26-0203: 
 
a. §190-271: To waive the requirement to provide a site plan for 
a conditional use application. 
 
As per RSA 674:36(II)(N), RSA 674:44(III)(e), and §190-148(D), 
Strict conformity would pose an unnecessary hardship to the 
Applicant and the waiver would not be contrary to the spirit and 
intent of the regulations; and specific circumstances, or 
conditions of the land, and the waiver will properly carry out the 
spirit and intent of the regulations. 
 
SECONDED by Mr. Hirsch 
 
MOTION CARRIED 7-0 
 
MOTION by Mr. Green to approve New Business – Conditional Use 
Permit A26-0203. The Board finds that the application meets the 
Approval Criteria under §190-133(F) with the following conditions: 
 
a) All outstanding comments from the Engineering Department 
shall be addressed to the satisfaction of the Division of 
Public Works. 
 
SECONDED by Ald. Klee 
 
MOTION CARRIED 7-0 
 
OTHER BUSINESS 
 
1. Review of tentative agenda to determine proposals of regional 
impact. 
 
MOTION by Mr. Zoller that there are no items of regional impact 
 
SECONDED by Mr. Varley   
 
MOTION CARRIED 7-0 
 
2. Appoint Board Member to the Nashua Regional Planning Commission 
Executive Committee 
 
Tabled to the December 3, 2026 meeting
NCPB 
November 19, 2026 
Page 9 
 
3. Appoint Board Member to the Historic District Commission 
 
Tabled to the December 3, 2026 meeting 
 
4. 2027 Meeting and Deadline Dates 
 
MOTION by Mr. Green to accept the Meeting and Deadline Dates, with 
the amendment that the July 1st meeting be changed to July 15th  
 
SECONDED by Mr. Hirsch   
 
MOTION CARRIED 7-0 
 
DISCUSSION ITEMS 
 
Land Use Code Criteria: Mr. Muise presented on the criteria for 
case approvals. 
 
MOTION to adjourn by Ald. Klee at 8:32 PM 
 
MOTION CARRIED 7-0 
 
PARTIAL DIGITAL RECORDING OF THIS MEETING IS AVAILABLE FOR 
LISTENING DURING REGULAR OFFICE HOURS. DIGITAL COPY OF AUDIO OF 
THE MEETING MAY BE MADE AVAILABLE UPON 48 HOURS ADVANCED NOTICE 
AND PAYMENT OF THE FEE. 
 
Kate Poirier – Taped Hearing
